sections.content: Colorado Springs has quietly become one of the most attractive markets for real estate investors in the Mountain West. Sitting at the base of Pikes Peak, the city combines strong military employment, a growing tech sector, and a steady stream of new residents from pricier Colorado cities like Denver and Boulder. Whether you are hunting wholesale deals, fix-and-flip opportunities, or long-term rentals, finding the right real estate deals in Colorado Springs CO requires knowing the local landscape inside and out. If you are just getting started, check out our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving in — it will give you the foundational knowledge to evaluate everything covered here.
Colorado Springs Market Overview: What Investors Need to Know in 2024

Colorado Springs is Colorado's second-largest city with a population of roughly 500,000 people — and it keeps growing. The city added more than 15,000 new residents between 2020 and 2023, driven largely by remote workers, military families stationed at Fort Carson and Peterson Space Force Base, and people priced out of Denver. That steady population growth creates consistent housing demand, which is exactly what investors want to see.

The median home price in Colorado Springs sits around $410,000 as of mid-2024, down roughly 8% from the 2022 peak of approximately $445,000. This correction has created real opportunity for investors who were sitting on the sidelines. Distressed sellers who bought at peak prices, landlords dealing with deferred maintenance, and out-of-state owners who inherited properties are all generating motivated-seller leads across the metro area. Explore active opportunities in the [Colorado Springs market](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/colorado-springs-co) to see current deal flow in the area.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Colorado Springs
Not every zip code in Colorado Springs makes sense for every strategy. Here is a breakdown of the neighborhoods that consistently produce strong investor returns across different deal types.
East Colorado Springs — Best for Wholesale and Flip Deals

The east side of the city, particularly around Academy Boulevard and Powers Boulevard, offers some of the highest concentrations of distressed properties in the metro. Median home prices here range from $280,000 to $340,000, making the numbers work for both wholesalers assigning contracts and flippers looking for 70% ARV deals. Renovation costs tend to run $25 to $45 per square foot for cosmetic updates in this area, and ARVs on updated 3-bed, 2-bath homes commonly land between $330,000 and $375,000.
Fountain and Security-Widefield — Best for Buy-and-Hold Rentals

Just south of Colorado Springs proper, Fountain and Security-Widefield sit adjacent to Fort Carson and attract a reliable base of military renters. Single-family homes in these areas typically list between $290,000 and $360,000, and rents for a 3-bedroom home average $1,600 to $1,900 per month. That rent-to-price ratio is one of the better ones you will find anywhere in the Front Range corridor.
Old Colorado City and Manitou Springs — Best for Short-Term Rentals

These historic neighborhoods near Pikes Peak and Garden of the Gods see heavy tourist traffic year-round. Investors running short-term rentals through platforms like Airbnb report gross annual revenues of $45,000 to $65,000 on well-managed properties. Keep in mind that Colorado Springs does require short-term rental permits, and regulations have tightened in recent years, so verify current rules before purchasing.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Colorado Springs

items: Wholesale deals: Colorado Springs has an active wholesaler community, and the east side produces frequent off-market leads from absentee owners, pre-foreclosures, and probate situations. Assignment fees typically range from $8,000 to $20,000 depending on the property and ARV.

Fix-and-flip: The correction from 2022 peak prices has restored flip margins. Experienced flippers targeting the east side and Fountain report net profits of $30,000 to $60,000 on well-executed projects when they buy at 65-70% of ARV minus repairs.

Long-term rentals: Military demand keeps vacancy rates low — typically under 5% metro-wide. Single-family rentals near Fort Carson and Peterson SFB attract stable, credit-screened tenants with steady income.

BRRRR strategy: The combination of relatively affordable distressed properties and strong rental demand makes Colorado Springs a solid BRRRR (Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat) market. Many investors are recycling capital through this method successfully.
Short-term rentals: Tourism near Pikes Peak, Garden of the Gods, and the U.S. Olympic Training Center supports strong short-term rental occupancy, especially from April through October.

Local Market Trends Shaping Deal Flow Right Now

Several trends are actively creating investor opportunity across Colorado Springs in 2024. First, mortgage rate pressure has pushed more homeowners into financial stress. The city saw a 22% increase in pre-foreclosure filings in the first half of 2024 compared to the same period in 2022, creating a fresh pipeline of motivated sellers. Second, the city's tech sector is expanding — defense contractors and space-industry companies are hiring, which is pushing rental demand upward in the northeast part of the metro around Powers Boulevard and Airport Road. Third, new construction is slowing. Homebuilders pulled back permits significantly in 2023, which will tighten resale inventory over the next 12 to 18 months and likely push prices upward again — good news for investors who buy now.

The best time to buy real estate in a recovering market is when most investors are still nervous. Colorado Springs has the fundamentals — population growth, military stability, and a diversifying economy — that reward patient, data-driven investors who act while others hesitate.
How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals in Colorado Springs

The most profitable real estate deals in Colorado Springs CO rarely appear on the MLS. The real money is made off-market, where you can negotiate directly with motivated sellers before the property is exposed to retail buyers. Understanding [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) is the single highest-leverage skill you can develop as a Colorado Springs investor. Common off-market lead sources in this market include direct mail campaigns targeting absentee owners in zip codes 80905, 80909, and 80910, driving for dollars in older neighborhoods like Stratmoor and Knob Hill, probate court records at the El Paso County courthouse, and building relationships with local wholesalers who work the Springs regularly.
Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Colorado Springs

Colorado Springs attracts significant interest from out-of-state investors — particularly from California, Texas, and Illinois — drawn by the city's relative affordability and growth trajectory. But investing remotely without local knowledge is a fast way to lose money. Here is how to approach this market intelligently from a distance.

items: Build your boots-on-the-ground team first: Find a local investor-friendly real estate agent, a property manager with experience in military rentals, and a general contractor before you make an offer. Ask for references and verify their track record.

Understand El Paso County's property tax rates: Colorado's property taxes are relatively low compared to national averages — El Paso County's effective rate runs about 0.49% — which helps cash flow on rental properties significantly.

Account for Colorado's climate in your rehab budgets: Roofs, HVAC systems, and foundations take more stress at altitude with extreme temperature swings. Budget 10-15% more for renovation contingency than you would in a milder climate.

Use data tools to analyze deals remotely: Learning [how to analyze real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) with reliable comps and deal calculators is especially critical when you cannot visit a property in person before making an offer.

Visit at least once before buying: Even a 2-day trip to walk neighborhoods, meet your team, and see the property stock firsthand will save you from expensive mistakes. The east side and west side of Colorado Springs feel like completely different markets.

sections.content: Getting Started with Wholesaling in Colorado Springs

For investors who want to start building deal flow without significant capital, wholesaling is an excellent entry point in this market. Colorado Springs has an established investor community hungry for quality deals, which means a solid contract on a distressed property can be assigned quickly for a fee. Before you start making offers, read up on [wholesaling real estate for beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) to understand the legal requirements, contract language, and marketing strategies that produce consistent deal flow in a competitive market like the Springs.

When targeting Colorado Springs wholesale deals, focus your direct mail on absentee owners who purchased before 2010 and have owned for more than 10 years. These owners often have significant equity, deferred maintenance, and motivation to sell — the perfect combination for a win-win wholesale deal.

Colorado Springs checks nearly every box that experienced real estate investors look for: population growth, military stability, a recovering price environment, strong rental demand, and a growing supply of motivated sellers. The investors who will profit most are those who do their homework, build local relationships, and move decisively when the numbers work. Whether you are chasing your first wholesale deal or building a rental portfolio, this market has the depth and diversity to support multiple strategies simultaneously.
